title: Equivariant constant extension preserving local curve pencils
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, $S$ a normal integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, $K=k(S)$, and $f:X\to S$ an H-projective morphism with $X$ integral of finite type over $k$. Assume all geometric fibres of $f$ are pure of dimension one and $C=X_K$ is smooth and geometrically integral. Put $F=k(X)$. Let $M\subset C$ be a reduced finite etale closed subscheme, and let a finite group $H$ act compatibly on $k,X,S,f$, preserving $M$; the actions may be nonfaithful and semilinear on $k$. Fix a prime $\ell\geq5$ different from $\operatorname{char}k$, and put $B=K^H$. There exist finite extensions $E_0/K$ and $K_0/E_0$ inside a common algebraic closure, with $E_0/K$ separable and $K_0/B$ Galois, such that $K_0$ contains a primitive $\ell$th root of unity. Define
$$H_0=\{(h,\sigma)\in H\times\operatorname{Aut}_B(K_0):\sigma|_K=h|_K\},\qquad A_0=\ker(H_0\to H).$$
The projection $H_0\to H$ is surjective and $K_0^{A_0}=K$. The tensor product $F_0=F\otimes_KK_0$ is a field with $F_0/F$ finite separable. Put $S_0=\operatorname{Nor}_{K_0}(S)$ and $X_0=\operatorname{Nor}_{F_0}(X)$. The base $S_0$ is normal integral projective of finite type over $k$, $S_0\to S$ is finite surjective, and $X_0\to X\times_SS_0$ is finite surjective. The scheme $X_0$ is normal integral of finite type over $k$, and $X_0\to S_0$ is H-projective with pure one-dimensional geometric fibres and generic fibre $C\times_KK_0$. The action
$$(h,\sigma)(z\otimes c)=h(z)\otimes\sigma(c)$$
extends uniquely to these models, compatibly with the given actions through $H_0\to H$: the morphisms $S_0\to S$, $X_0\to X$, $X_0\to S_0$ and $X_0\to X\times_SS_0$ are equivariant. Moreover $F_0^{A_0}=F$. Writing $S_{E_0}=\operatorname{Nor}_{E_0}(S)$ and $X_{E_0}=\operatorname{Nor}_{FE_0}(X)$, there is a finite affine cover $S_{E_0}=\bigcup_iV_i$ and finite surjective pencils $\psi_i:(X_{E_0})_{V_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{V_i}$. There is a finite map $X_0\to X_{E_0}$ over $S_0\to S_{E_0}$, and the induced pencils $\varphi_i:(X_0)_{U_i}\to\mathbf P^1_{U_i}$, where $U_i=S_0\times_{S_{E_0}}V_i$, are finite surjective. The opens $U_i$ form a finite affine cover of $S_0$. Their generic fibres are generically etale and their inverse images of $0,1,\infty$ are reduced finite etale over $K_0$, disjoint from the reduced inverse image $M_0$ of $M$. The marking $M_0$ is finite etale and $H_0$-stable. If $\dim S>0$, $E_0$ may be chosen equal to $K$; if $\dim S=0$, one open suffices. No invariance of individual pencils under $H_0$ is required.

Normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain. H-projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target. A finite separable field extension is finite-dimensional with separable minimal polynomials. A finite Galois extension is a finite normal separable extension; normal for fields means that every irreducible polynomial over the smaller field with a root in the larger field splits there. For a group $G$ acting on a field $V$, $V^G$ is the subfield of elements fixed by every member of $G$. All fixed-field equalities below use the field embeddings induced by the displayed scheme maps. A primitive $\ell$th root of unity is an element of multiplicative order $\ell$. A finite morphism of integral curves is generically etale when it is etale over a dense open subset of its target. The notions used are [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-pure-dimension], [def-weil-geometric-fibre], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible], [def-fin-normalization-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change], [def-weil-algebraic-closure].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-invariant-local-curve-pencils] with $J=\{1\}$, acting trivially on $X$ over $S$. All its geometric hypotheses are exactly the hypotheses here, and every marking is stable under this trivial group. Obtain its finite separable extension $E_0/K$, affine cover $V_i$ of $S_{E_0}$, and finite surjective pencils $\psi_i$. Their generic fibres are generically etale, their three special fibres are finite etale and avoid $M_{E_0}$. The cited lemma gives $E_0=K$ when $\dim S>0$ and a single open when $\dim S=0$. No condition involving the original group $H$ has been imposed on these pencils. Apply the constant-extension case of [lem-sfb-finite-normal-relative-curve-model] to $E_0/K$: $FE_0=F\otimes_KE_0$ is a field, and $X_{E_0}/S_{E_0}$ has the normal integral, projectivity, finite-type, pure-fibre and smooth geometrically integral generic-fibre properties needed below.

proof.text: Choose a separable closure $\Omega/E_0$ using [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois]. Put $q(T)=1+T+\cdots+T^{\ell-1}$. This polynomial is nonconstant and coprime to its derivative: modulo any common divisor of $q,q^{\prime}$, differentiating $(T-1)q=T^\ell-1$ gives $\ell T^{\ell-1}=0$, while $T^\ell=1$; this forces the common divisor to be a unit because $\ell$ is invertible. The defining root property in [def-pc-separably-closed] gives a root $\zeta\in\Omega$. Since $q(1)=\ell\ne0$ and $(\zeta-1)q(\zeta)=\zeta^\ell-1$, we have $\zeta\ne1$ and $\zeta^\ell=1$. Primality of $\ell$ makes its order exactly $\ell$. By [lem-weil-pbc-simple-algebraic-extension-power-basis], $D=E_0(\zeta)$ is finite over $E_0$. The intermediate-subfield clause of the separable-closure lemma makes $D/E_0$ separable. Consequently $D/K$ is finite separable: finiteness follows by multiplying two finite spanning bases and separability by [lem-zl-separable-permanence].

proof.text: Apply the separable case of [lem-sfb-finite-semilinear-field-envelope] to the given action $H\to\operatorname{Aut}(K)$ and the finite separable extension $D/K$. Its field $M$ is our $K_0$ and its compatible-pair group $J$ is exactly the displayed $H_0$. It gives $K_0/B$ finite Galois, $K_0/K$ finite Galois, the surjection $H_0\to H$, and $K_0^{A_0}=K$. Its tower contains $D$ and hence $E_0$ and $\zeta$. Moreover $K_0/E_0$ is finite separable: a finite spanning set over $K$ spans over $E_0$, and [lem-sfb-separable-algebraic-intermediate-base] supplies separability. Embed this finite tower into an algebraic closure of $E_0$, fixing $E_0$, by [lem-weil-pbc-algebraic-extension-embeds-algebraically-closed]. This preserves the chosen $E_0$ and its pencils.

proof.text: The constant-extension clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normal-relative-curve-model], applied now to $E=K_0$, says that its hypotheses on $L,E,C$ hold for $L=F\otimes_KK_0$. Thus $F_0$ is a field, $F_0/F$ is finite separable, and the generic curve is $C\times_KK_0$. The same lemma supplies $S_0,X_0$ with all the required normality, integrality, finite-type and H-projectivity properties, the finite surjection $S_0\to S$, the finite surjection $X_0\to X\times_SS_0$, the pure one-dimensional geometric fibres, and the asserted generic-fibre identification.

proof.text: For $(h,\sigma)\in H_0$, the proposed tensor action respects balancing: the images of $az\otimes c$ and $z\otimes ac$, for $a\in K$, agree because $h(a)=\sigma(a)$. It preserves sums and products on pure tensors, its inverse is the map for $(h^{-1},\sigma^{-1})$, and composing two such maps gives the componentwise group product. Hence it is an action by field automorphisms of $F_0$, extending both prescribed field actions. By the functoriality and uniqueness clause of [lem-sfb-finite-normal-relative-curve-model], it extends uniquely to $X_0,S_0$, including when the actions move $k$. The four structural maps in the statement commute with these actions, since they are the canonical maps of that functorial construction. The left field action is understood as inverse pullback on schemes, so no reversal of the group product is involved.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-tensor-kernel-inseparable-invariants] with its base field $K$, left field $F$, right field $K_0$, acting group $N=H_0$, and normal subgroup $Q=A_0$. Its auxiliary subfield may be $R=F^H$, since $H_0/A_0$ acts on $F$ exactly through $H$ and $F^H/R$ is the identity extension. The subgroup $A_0$ fixes $F$ pointwise; its fixed field on the right is $K$ by step 3, an identity purely inseparable extension. The tensor algebra is a field by step 4. The cited equality therefore reads $F_0^{A_0}=F\otimes_KK=F$, with the identification $z\otimes a\mapsto za$ and inverse $z\mapsto z\otimes1$. These are the embeddings of the scheme diagram.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-finite-normal-relative-curve-model] a second time to $X_{E_0}\to S_{E_0}$ and $K_0/E_0$. The constant-extension tensor is canonically $F_0$, by $((z\otimes a)\otimes b)\mapsto z\otimes ab$, with inverse $z\otimes b\mapsto(z\otimes1)\otimes b$. Let the resulting models be $Y,T$. The composites $Y\to X_{E_0}\to X$ and $T\to S_{E_0}\to S$ are finite surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-composition] and pointwise surjectivity. They are normal integral, with function fields $F_0,K_0$, respectively, and locally Noetherian by finite type over $k$ and [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. By [lem-sfb-finite-normal-cover-normalization] they identify canonically with $X_0,S_0$, inducing the identity on those fields. Thus the second application supplies a finite surjection $X_0\to X_{E_0}\times_{S_{E_0}}S_0$ and a finite surjection $S_0\to S_{E_0}$. The projections give the desired finite map $X_0\to X_{E_0}$. For each $i$, base change $\psi_i$ to $U_i=S_0\times_{S_{E_0}}V_i$ and compose with the finite surjection just obtained; this defines $\varphi_i$. The base-changed pencil is finite by [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and surjective by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change], applied on its affine target charts. Composition preserves these properties. Each $U_i$ is affine because it is the inverse image of an affine under the finite morphism $S_0\to S_{E_0}$, as in [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Preimages of the finite covering $V_i$ cover $S_0$. A single $V_i$ still gives a single $U_i$.

source.place: §§3.2--3.5, printed pp.605--606; agent assembly of the cited DAG statements. Publisher PDF read online; local PDF WANTED.

proof.text: On generic fibres the intermediate-model map of step 7 is the identity of $C\times_KK_0$ under the tensor isomorphism displayed there. Hence the generic $\varphi_i$ is precisely the base change of the generic $\psi_i$. Its etale open stays etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change] and nonempty by [lem-weil-pbc-spec-surjective-base-change] on affine charts. Its fibres above $0,1,\infty$, and the marking $M_0=M\times_KK_0$, are finite by finite base-change stability [lem-trf-finite-radicial-basechange] and etale by etale base-change stability. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-fibre-discrete-separable-points], an etale scheme over a field is a disjoint union of spectra of separable fields, hence reduced. Thus these are the reduced fibres and reduced inverse-image marking requested. Their intersections with $M_0$ are empty because they are base changes of the empty intersections in step 1. The diagonal action preserves $M_0$: it takes a pair lying above $M$ to one lying above $h(M)=M$; reduction preserves that closed subset. No pencil invariance is required. Together with steps 1--7 this proves every clause.
